site.sitedescription: The  surrounding  vegetation  is  classified  as  low open woodland and tall shrubland (4–10 m), an alliance of Eucalyptus signata, E. gummifera and Banksia  aemula (Coutts 1994).  The  younger  dune  systems  to  the  north  and  south  carry open  forest  to  30  m,  an  alliance  of  E.  pilularis,  Syncarpia  hillii  and  Allocasuarina  torulosa (Coutts 1994). Notophyll vine forest, simple notophyll vine forest and simple microphyll vine forest (Backhousia myrtifolia) (Young and McDonald 1987) are concentrated on sedimentary unit  ‘Qpb’,  along  gullies  and  areas  where  the  water-table  comes  close  to  the  surface  and  attopographically  sheltered  locations  (Coutts  1994).  These  areas  were  originally  inState  forest  and  were  extensively  logged  for  Araucaria  cunninghamii,  Agathis  robusta, Syncarpia  hillii and Eucalyptus  pilularis before  the  Island  became  a  World  Heritage  area (Young and McDonald 1987).
